title: Statutory and Larkspur Late-Booking Interest Rates for Closing and Funding Refunds
content:
**Terms.** The refund deadline of a Closing and Funding late-funding refund is the last of the closing method's per diem refund business days, counted Monday through Friday starting with the day after the disbursement date; the per diem refund business days are 10 under every closing method. A late-funding refund is booked late when its booking date falls after that deadline.

The late-booking interest rate of a late-funding refund is set from the booking date and the closing's property state:

| Booking date | Closing's property state | Late-booking interest rate |
|---|---|---|
| after the refund deadline | CA, CT, IL, MD or NY | 6.0 percent a year |
| after the refund deadline | any other state | 4.0 percent a year |
| on or before the refund deadline | any state | no late-booking interest rate (zero) |

## The late-booking interest

Any late-booking interest owed on a late-funding refund is added to it, the interest rounded half up to the cent on its own. The late-booking interest is the late-funding refund before interest times the late-booking interest rate taken as a percent, times the late-booking interest days, divided by the per diem day-count basis (365 under every closing method), rounded half up to the cent. Apart from the late-booking interest a late-funding refund carries, a late-funding dispute earns no compensation beyond the interest refund.

Hypothetical: a refund of 156.15 before interest, at 6.0 percent a year over 13 late-booking interest days, gives 156.15 times 6.0 percent, times 13, divided by 365, which is 0.33 after rounding; the refund entry carries 156.48.

## The deadline on both sides (hypothetical dates)

A loan disbursed on Wednesday the 3rd: business day 1 is Thursday the 4th and business day 10 is Wednesday the 17th, so the refund deadline is the 17th.

| Booked on | Booked late? | Rate for a property in IL | Rate for a property in OH |
|---|---|---|---|
| the 17th | No | none | none |
| the 18th | Yes | 6.0 percent a year | 4.0 percent a year |
